canonical_statement: For every suitable weak solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, its singular set has zero one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure.
domain_and_universes: SpaceTime = (Fin 3 -> Real) x Real; Velocity = Fin 3 -> Real; all data and semantic interfaces live in Lean Type/Prop universe 0.
hypotheses: S.IsSuitableWeakSolution D, carrying the source's distributional Navier-Stokes equation, incompressibility, velocity/pressure integrability, local energy inequality, and local-domain clauses
conclusion: S.ParabolicHausdorffOneMeasureZero {z | z is in D.domain and not S.RegularAt D z}.
encoding_boundary: The pinned snapshot has no canonical suitable-weak-solution, CKN regular-point, or parabolic Hausdorff-measure API. CKNSourceSemantics parameterizes exactly these source notions without assuming any theorem conclusion or proof witness. This is a semantic statement interface: the later source-audit and proof phases must instantiate and transport it to concrete analytic definitions before root proof credit is possible.

smooth-solution regularity in place of suitable weak solutions
a package with the conclusion stored as an assumed proof field
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: The statement adds no force-free, bounded-domain, global-existence, or smoothness hypothesis. The singular set is restricted to D.domain. If it is empty, the same parabolic-measure predicate remains the conclusion; no Euclidean surrogate or automatic empty-set lemma is postulated here.
